+title: Add update checks and automatic update to MarketplaceStore (no built-in times)
+---
+## What
+
+marketplace.md §8 and decisions 13 and 15. The package has no built-in time value. A check runs at `start()` and on request. A periodic check runs only when the host gives an interval.
+
+In `Sources/FoundationModelsSkills/Marketplace/MarketplaceStore.swift` and `MarketplacePolicy.swift`:
+- `MarketplacePolicy`: `checkInterval: Duration?` (default `nil`), `autoUpdate: Bool` (default `true`), `checkOnly: Bool` (default `false`), `applyUpdates: ApplyUpdates` (`.immediately` default, `.nextLaunch`), `fetchTimeout: Duration?` (default `nil`), and the `SnapshotLimits`. `SKILLS_MARKETPLACE_AUTOUPDATE=0` in the environment has the same effect as `autoUpdate: false`.
+- `func check() async -> [MarketplaceStatus]`: one `remoteHead` for each git source. It publishes `.checked`, and `.updateAvailable` when the head differs. It never fetches.
+- **Coalescing:** while a check or update of a marketplace is in progress, another request for it waits for the same `Task`. No second remote connection.
+- `start()`: check each source. Update it when `autoUpdate` is on, the source has no pin, and `checkOnly` is off. Otherwise publish `.updateAvailable`.
+- Pins: `pin(_:sha:)` and `unpin(_:)` store `pinnedSha` in `state.json`. A `sha:` field on the source also pins it. A pinned source never updates automatically, and `check()` still reports a newer head.
+- `.nextLaunch`: materialize the new snapshot, store it as pending in `state.json`, and swap `current` only at the next `start()`.
+- Interval: only when `checkInterval` is not `nil`, a loop checks at that interval until `stop()`. The internal init takes a clock (`any Clock<Duration>`), so tests use a manual clock and no real wait.
+
+- [ ] `MarketplacePolicy` fields and the environment switch
+- [ ] `check()` with coalescing
+- [ ] Update rules at `start()`: auto, off, `checkOnly`, pins
+- [ ] `.nextLaunch`
+- [ ] The optional interval loop and `stop()`
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] With the default policy, `start()` makes one remote-head call for each source, and no later call happens until a request comes
+- [ ] Two concurrent `check()` calls make one remote-head call
+- [ ] Pinned, `autoUpdate: false`, and `checkOnly` sources publish `.updateAvailable` and never fetch
+- [ ] With `.nextLaunch`, `current` changes only after the next `start()`
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsSkillsTests/MarketplaceUpdateTests.swift` with the counting `GitTransport` double and a manual clock: default policy (no later calls); coalesced checks; auto-update fetch; `autoUpdate: false`; `checkOnly`; the environment switch; a pin through the source and through `pin(_:sha:)`; `.nextLaunch`; the interval loop advances only when the manual clock advances; `stop()` ends the loop
+- [ ] Run `swift test --filter MarketplaceUpdateTests`; then `swift test`; all green
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file

+  text: |-
+    Research: marketplace.md §8.1 to §8.3 and decisions 13 and 15 give the shape. §6.2 pins the event cases: `.checked(id:current:latest:)` and `.updateAvailable(id:from:to:)`. `MarketplaceEvent` held only `.updated` and `.failed`, thus both cases are new here. `current` and `from` are optional, as `.updated(from:)` already is: a cold marketplace holds no snapshot yet.
+
+    Design of the store:
+    - One `PassKind` (`.check` or `.update(force:)`) per request. `resolved(_:)` turns an update into a check when `checkOnly` is on, thus the dry run never fetches, also for an explicit `update()`.
+    - Coalescing: `inFlight[index]` holds the task of the pass that runs now, with an id. A new request joins it when `PassKind.answers(_:)` says the running pass answers it; an update answers a check, a check answers no update. The task takes itself out of the table before it ends, thus a joiner that wakes later starts a pass of its own and no loop spins.
+    - The interval loop sleeps on the injected clock, thus the package holds no interval. `stop()` cancels the loop and each pass that runs now.
+    - `fetchTimeout` runs the fetch and one clock sleep in a task group. The first to end wins; the sleep gives `MarketplaceTimeoutError`, which the failure path turns into `.failed` with `keptVersion`.
+
+    Test support (`MarketplaceUpdateTestSupport.swift`): a `ManualClock` (a `Clock` over a `Mutex`, with a sleep count and a wait for a sleeper), a `GatedGitTransport` that wraps another transport and holds a call until the test releases it or the task is cancelled, a `MarketplaceEventLog`, and a `TestSignal`. The gate wraps `RecordingGitTransport`, thus no count is written twice.
